evidence: Cic. N.D. 3.24: cursūs certī et cōnstantēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Standing firm: of the courses of the stars, of a steady face and step (cōnstantī vultū graduque, Liv. 5.46.3), of a friend who does not change. It also means consistent, agreeing with itself: cōnstāns fāma, a report everyone gives alike (Lewis & Short). The noun is cōnstantia.
Firm on its feet, and so lasting; Cicero pairs it with cōnstāns of friends.
Even and uniform: a steady motion, a river that flows at the same rate, a temper that does not change (Lewis & Short). It also means fair, treating all alike.

evidence: Caes. BG 4.33: mōbilitātem equitum, stabilitātem peditum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The noun of stabilis: firmness of footing, and the lasting steadiness of fortune or friendship.

phrases.latin: sunt igitur firmī et stabilēs et cōnstantēs ēligendī, cujus generis est magna pēnūria
phrases.english: so we must choose friends who are firm, steady and constant, and of that kind there is a great shortage

phrases.latin: praeclāraque est aequābilitās in omnī vītā et īdem semper vultus eademque frōns
phrases.english: and a fine thing is evenness all through life: always the same face, the same brow
